q1.prompt: A text editor must store actions for undo, redo, keyboard shortcuts, and macros. Which representation fits?

choices.label: Command objects that carry action data and execute against the document
Direct UI callbacks with no stored action value

wrong1.prompt: A direct call leaves no action to manage later.
wrong1.explanation: Undo, redo, queuing, and macros need the request to exist as data. Command makes the action and its arguments a first-class value.

q2.prompt: DeleteRange(1, 2) removes “at” from “cat”. What must the command retain to support undo?

choices.label: The start position and removed text so undo can restore “at”
Only the method name delete; the old data is unnecessary

wrong2.explanation: A reversible command must capture enough information to restore what changed. The operation name alone cannot reconstruct the deleted characters.

q3.prompt: A queued ChargeCard command may be delivered twice after a worker crash. What completes the design?

choices.label: A stable command id checked durably so redelivery does not charge twice
Assume the queue delivers exactly once and omit deduplication

wrong3.explanation: At-least-once delivery can repeat a command after an ambiguous failure. Persisting the command id with the charge makes the repeated execution safe.

success.prompt: You represented actions as data, captured undo state, and made a retried command idempotent.
